subject: Pilot metrics & ownership — SapphireAI evaluation runway
body:
Message 1 — From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <james.park@sapphireai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot metrics & ownership — SapphireAI evaluation runway

Thanks again for the productive demo earlier today — appreciate the clarity on the primary product flows we need to validate. Per our call, I captured an initial, pragmatic set of success metrics and the minimal evaluation plan so we can get a short, deterministic pilot (2-3 week runway) that answers your key questions. Attaching a simple metrics template that we can iterate on.

High-level POC goal
- Validate feasibility of integrating Redwood Inference into SapphireAI’s answer-generation pipeline with predictable latency, acceptable unit cost, and demonstrable quality on your business prompts.

Proposed success criteria (draft)
- Latency: P95 end-to-end request latency <= 350 ms for 512-token prompts under steady-state load.
- Throughput: steady-state 30 req/s with ability to absorb 60 req/s bursts for short windows (1–2 minutes).
- Cost: nominal inference cost <= $0.0015/token (target average across mixed prompt lengths) with visibility into per-route cost.
- Quality: automated pass rate >= 88% on curated evaluation set (N=200), and <= 1 critical hallucination per 500 responses on the safety checklist.
- Reliability: <= 1% error rate (5xx/4xx) during the test window.

Evaluation plan (high level)
- Week 0: Prep & access — share workload spec + sample prompt corpus (you provide), Redwood provides test harness and simple synthetic load script.
- Week 1: Smoke + validation — deploy model variant, run smoke, capture latency/throughput under small load.
- Week 2: Production-ish run — run 48-hour sustained evaluation with blended traffic, collect token-level cost & quality metrics; run human eval on a 200-item heldout set.
- Tie-breaker: If automated metrics are close to threshold, we’ll run a short A/B human comparison (50 live queries each).

Owners / roles
- Redwood (Soji/Ben): infra provisioning, model selection, runbook for load tests, cost profiling.
- Sapphire (James/Anita): provide sample corpus, accept/reject criteria for quality, and point person for test-window schedule.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) James: please upload the prompt corpus + 10 representative long prompts to the Drive link by Tue 10/5.
2) Ben: can you confirm available dedicated capacity windows next week and preferred quantization profile?
3) I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Wed 10/6 to agree final metrics and the 48-hour run cadence.

Attachments: sapphire-pilot-metrics-template.xlsx, example-workload-spec.json

—
Soojin Lee
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

-----

Message 2 — From: James Park <james.park@sapphireai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anita Desai <anita@sapphireai.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot metrics & ownership — SapphireAI evaluation runway

Thanks Soojin — this captures the core asks well. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency: the 350 ms P95 target is reasonable for short prompts. For longer prompts (~1k tokens) we understand latency will increase; please call out how Redwood reports latency by prompt-length buckets.
- Throughput: our primary burst mode is during scheduled batch enrichment; the numbers you suggested (30 steady / 60 burst) map to our internal estimates.
- Cost: the $0.0015/token average is aggressive but acceptable for the POC if we can get precise per-route cost breakdowns. We want a breakdown by model variant and quantization option.
- Quality: we’ll run the 200-item human eval. Our quality criteria: at least 90% accept rate rather than 88% — we can relax to 88% if there’s a clear latency/cost tradeoff. Also request that you add a small safety test set (N=50) that captures hallucination-sensitive prompts.

We’ll upload the prompt corpus by Tue 10/5 EOD. Can you confirm the kickoff time on 10/6? We prefer morning PT.

Cheers,
James Park
Head of Platform, SapphireAI
james.park@sapphireai.com

-----

Message 3 — From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Park <james.park@sapphireai.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 10:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot metrics & ownership — SapphireAI evaluation runway

Looping in a couple of infra/ops notes that will affect run cadence and owners:

- Capacity: We have a dedicated pool we can reserve for the 48-hour run, but need a confirmed 48-hr window 72 hours in advance. Suggest Wed 10/13 — Fri 10/15 as options.
- Quantization & performance knobs: propose two configs to test: fp16 (baseline) and 4-bit quantized (Q4_0) to check the cost/latency tradeoffs. I’ll run initial microbenchmarks to estimate token-level cost delta.
- Caching: Redwood can enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts; that will materially reduce cost for some workflows. Need Sapphire to mark which calls are cacheable.

Operational asks
- Rachel: can you prepare the load harness and a small synthetic dataset to validate throughput targets? Aim for a 1-hour load test first, then escalate to the 48-hour window.
- Soojin: can you confirm we’ll expose per-route token metrics to James (token counts, model, quantization flag) in the dashboard?

I’ll attach a short runbook after we confirm the exact 48-hour slot.

—
Ben Carter
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

-----

Message 4 — From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <james.park@sapphireai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Oct 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot metrics & ownership — SapphireAI evaluation runway

Thanks James — we’re aligned. Quick summary & confirmed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks: 

Confirmed metrics (finalized)
- Latency: P95 <= 350 ms for <=512-token prompts; metrics will be bucketed by prompt-length (<=256, 257-512, 513-1024).
- Throughput: steady 30 req/s, burst to 60 req/s (1–2 minute windows).
- Cost: target avg <= $0.0015/token; we’ll present a per-model/quantization breakdown.
- Quality: target 90% human accept rate on the 200-item set; safety set (N=50) must have <=1 critical hallucination.

Confirmed owners & short timeline
- Soojin (Redwood): primary solutions lead — kickoff, metrics sign-off, human eval coordination.
- Ben (Redwood): infra and runbook owner — reserved capacity, perf tuning, quantization tests.
- Rachel (Redwood): load harness + dashboard instrumentation.
- James / Anita (Sapphire): corpus upload, accept/reject adjudication, schedule confirmation.

Immediate calendar items
- Kickoff: Wed 2027-10-06 09:30 PT (I’ve sent a calendar invite).
- Capacity windows: Ben will propose exact 48-hr slots by Tue 2027-10-11.
- Artifact drop: James to upload corpus by Tue 2027-10-05 EOD.

Deliverables we’ll share after kickoff
- Pilot metrics template (filled by Redwood)
- Short runbook for the 48-hour evaluation (Ben)
- Results dashboard link and token-level cost CSV after the run (Rachel)

If that matches your expectations, I’ll mark the plan as ’kickoff-ready’ and we’ll proceed with resource reservations.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

—
Soojin Lee
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
